data.name: tranche-workflow
data.description: ProjectMapper development runs in gated tranches journaled in .dev-log/; follow it for any implementation work
data.body:
All implementation follows the tranche workflow in `.dev-log/README.md` (gitignored, never read by the app):
entry record (plan position, current state, expected outcome, steps, not-building, stop conditions) →
step: enter / implement / review / record evidence → whole-tranche review/fix loop → closing outcome,
residual limits, next tranche title → PARKED → commit "Tranche N is parked." → fresh entry for next.

Rules the user holds to: record exact commands + observed results; never label a blocked or unexecuted
check as passed; supersede (don't erase) premature claims; historical entries are labeled historical;
plans live in `docs/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-name.md`, updated in place with a decision log; `.parts/` is
read-only disposable reference; `.dev-log/` has no runtime role. Plan review precedes implementation.

`.dev-log/` stays gitignored and local-only by owner decision (2026-09-23); don't propose committing it again.
Material decisions go in the plan's §17 decision log, not only the journal — the owner checks for full documentation.
At every status change (entry approved, step done, parked) update ALL status lines together: plan header, plan §2,
docs/README.md (its "Current state" section and phase history), .dev-log/README.md (status + "Resume point"), and the
tranche journal header. The owner approves each entry and step ("continue with N.x"); every push/release is a separate explicit approval.
Capture test exit codes without pipes masking them.

Why: the user asked (2026-09-23) that revival work "continue the same set of mechanics which left the project in the shape it is."
How to apply: open a journal entry before touching code for a tranche; park + commit at each tranche close.

data.name: vend-sanitization
data.description: Rules for any vended/published copy: only the owner's name in LICENSE.md; no handles, paths, or vendor/AI names
data.body:
When a copy of a project is vended or published, it must be sanitized:
- The owner's real name (Jacob Lambert) appears ONLY in LICENSE.md (MIT copyright). Nowhere else.
- The gaming handle must never appear; it leaked via global git config and sits on old commits. Do not carry that history into a vended copy.
- No local drive paths, usernames, emails, secrets, or private-journal pointers (.dev-log stays gitignored and unmentioned).
- No AI/vendor product names (Claude, Gemini, Codex, etc.): say "agent". No Co-Authored-By AI trailers in commits.
- Commit author metadata must carry some identity: ask the owner at vend time which neutral identity to use.

Why: owner decisions 2026-10-06 while publishing Episode 0.0 and planning the DataMAPPER handoff.
How to apply: at vend time, copy tracked content only, start a fresh single-commit history, run a scan for names/handles/paths/secrets/vendor terms over files and zip contents, and report hits before pushing. Pushes are always a separate explicit approval.

data.name: gui-probe-safety
data.description: GUI probes must never block the Tk event loop; PowerShell screen capture hangs — use ctypes GDI grabber
data.body:
Never run blocking work (subprocess.run, waits) inside a Tk callback in probe or demo scripts.
On 2026-09-23 a screenshot script did PowerShell CopyFromScreen inside root.after, the demo window showed "Not Responding" to the owner.

Window process stays responsive and self-closes (e.g. after(20000, destroy)); a separate orchestrator waits/captures with timeouts.
PowerShell System.Drawing.CopyFromScreen times out here — capture with ctypes GDI BitBlt (0.5s) instead.

A smoke test's real messagebox.showerror popped up on the owner's desktop during a background suite loop and blocked it.
Cause: event_generate key events only reach the focused window. Test GUI code must never depend on OS keyboard focus
(use DesktopCase.fire_binding in tests/test_ui_smoke.py) and must never be able to open a real modal (guard_modals).

Why: the owner sees every window opened; a hung window looks like the app is broken.
How to apply: window stays responsive; use ctypes GDI for screenshots; use guard_modals + fire_binding in tests.

data.name: feedback-cleanup-philosophy
data.description: User's priorities for cleanup and consolidation passes on ProjectMapper
data.body:
Consolidation first: reduce code size and complexity wherever possible without loss of function, integrity, or clean separation of concerns. Removing deprecated/unused systems falls under this.

Why: app.py is growing large; keeping it lean makes future work cheaper.
How to apply: before deleting anything, ask whether a planned future feature (git ops, tabbed toolbar, UI revamp) would want it. If uncertain, hold in a parts bin rather than hard-delete. When the answer is clearly no, remove it.

Bugs and frailties: identify cheap/easy wins. Don't skip things just because they're small.
UI/UX: make Tkinter look crisp and responsive. Apply trusted Tk best practices. Snappiness matters — slow or laggy interactions are a bug.
Approach: spawn an adversarial reviewer to read the code and produce a prioritized report before acting.

data.name: project-schematoucher
data.description: Design spec for SchemaTOUCHER — schema-driven record editor backed by a JSONL spine
data.body:
SchemaTOUCHER is a Tkinter tool window in ProjectMapper. A single window with two synchronized views of one in-memory JSON transformation object: a structured form on the left and a raw JSON editor on the right.

Fields: id, parent, origin (JSON), target (JSON), operation (JSON), result (JSON), status
Workflow: New/Open → Edit (form or raw JSON) → Validate → Save → Reopen (reconstructs from file)

Implementation rule: one in-memory model only. Form and JSON editor are two views. While raw JSON is invalid/incomplete, preserve the draft and don't let a form update silently overwrite it.

Existing machinery to reuse: ToolWindowMixin in tools/ui_base.py, text.open/text.save/file.create actions, TextToucher patterns, Text Editor dirty-state pattern.
Launch point: existing tree context menu.
Acceptance test: Open → create object → edit in either view → save → close → reopen → see exactly the same object.

Why: first proof of concept for constructing and persisting a structured transformation object inside ProjectMapper's existing toolchain.

data.name: project-complexity-review
data.description: 2026-10-31 adversarial complexity review findings — dead code, duplicate constants, decomposition targets
data.body:
Adversarial complexity review run 2026-10-31 against main (501 pass / 2 skip).

High-confidence cuts:
- core/helpers.py:90-105 get_folder_size_bytes — dead, no external caller
- tools/project_patcher.py:135-136 — double DiffFile construction; 4 SequenceMatcher passes where 1 suffices
- application/history.py:15 — duplicate TERMINAL constant; contracts.py already has it

Medium-confidence cuts:
- EXAMPLE_MANIFEST in project_patcher.py — used only by one test, not in controller
- write_text_file in snapshots.py — misplaced, non-atomic; inline or move to writes.py
- 28 section marker comment lines in app.py — no editor/test uses them
- _try_import in diagnostics.py — single-use, inline it
- Four 'from X import *' blocks in app.py — makes dead-symbol detection impossible; switch to explicit imports

Decomposition candidates (no new files needed):
- ProgressPopup (app.py:152-217) — already self-contained; move to tools/ui_base.py
- Scan→snapshot→export pipeline: 3 methods share the same 4-step shape; extract a _run_export orchestrator
- _setup_ui (lines 642-881): decompose into named sub-builders per UI zone

Backlog Pyright issues (no runtime risk): controller.py state.root used without None-guard; exports.py:98 SOURCE_ROOT None narrowing; app.py:1254 **_mb_kw dict unpacking.

Why: user requested adversarial complexity review to shrink codebase before further feature work.
How to apply: use findings to plan a cleanup tranche; highest-leverage first hit is the star-import fix in app.py; highest-yield deletion is get_folder_size_bytes.

data.name: session-2026-11-02-changes
data.description: Changes made in session aafae753: run-command feature, _ProjectMAPPER source fix, .spine→_spine rename, tab visibility fix
data.body:
Session aafae753-61f7-4544-be48-dfbbcd8d1cf6 (2026-11-02) made the following changes to ProjectMapper:

1. Run Command Here feature: right-click any folder in tree or folder content panel → 'Run Command Here…' opens RunCommandWindow with PowerShell command entry, streaming output, Up/Down history, Kill/Clear buttons. New file: tools/run_command.py. New tooltips in tools/tooltips.py. Registered in tools/__init__.py. Menu item added to _show_path_context_menu in app.py.

2. Folder content panel fixes: added <ButtonRelease-1> and <ButtonRelease-3> bindings to _content_grid_inner so that clicking empty space deselects icons and right-click shows context menu.

3. _ProjectMAPPER run.bat fixed: was pointing at _ProjectMAPPER/src (stale copy); updated PYTHONPATH to ../ProjectMapper/src so run.bat uses the live repo source. _ProjectMAPPER/src/ deleted (150 files removed).

4. .spine renamed to _spine to avoid .gitignore blanket exclusions. Two references in tools/schema_toucher_ui.py updated. Spine kept public (not gitignored).

5. Toolbar tab visibility: inactive Snapshot/Git tabs were same color as bar (heading_bg #2A3441). Changed inactive tab bg to success green (#2F8E6A) so tabs are visually distinct.

6. claude-memory.jsonl spine created: all 8 Claude session memory files translated into spine entries under claude-memory@1 schema.

data.name: feedback-spine-session-refs
data.description: Include session_ref field in spine entries tied to a specific conversation
data.body:
When appending entries to a .spine/*.jsonl file, add a session_ref field with the Claude Code session ID when the entry records a decision, implementation, or review that happened in a conversation.

Why: lets a future assistant trace why a decision was made — not just what was decided — by looking up the session transcript. The user confirmed this is the desired pattern (2026-10-31).
How to apply: include "session_ref": "<session-id>" in the data dict. The session ID is available from the working directory path or session context. Only add it when the entry is tied to a specific conversation; don't add it for entries that record purely technical state with no conversational context.
